tx-harris-2026-dist314-moore-michelle.bio: Presiding judge of the 314th District Court since 2019; former Harris County assistant county attorney and assistant district attorney in Cameron and Dallas counties.

tx-harris-2026-dist315-shapiro-leah.name: Leah Shapiro
tx-harris-2026-dist315-shapiro-leah.bio: Presiding judge of the 315th District Court since 2019; former prosecutor and assistant public defender.

tx-harris-2026-dist180-pierce-tami.name: Tami C. Pierce
tx-harris-2026-dist180-pierce-tami.bio: Former police officer, investigator and patrol sergeant who has worked as both a criminal defense attorney and a prosecutor.

tx-harris-2026-dist180-morales-stephanie.name: Stephanie Morales
tx-harris-2026-dist180-morales-stephanie.bio: Attorney with experience as both a prosecutor and a defense attorney.

tx-harris-2026-dist183-long-lance.name: Lance Long
tx-harris-2026-dist183-long-lance.bio: Judge of the 183rd District Court, appointed by Governor Greg Abbott in 2025; spent over two decades with the Harris County District Attorney’s Office.

tx-harris-2026-dist184-thomas-katherine.name: Katherine "Kat" Thomas
tx-harris-2026-dist184-thomas-katherine.bio: Judge of the 184th Criminal District Court; former Harris County prosecutor who teaches at Thurgood Marshall School of Law.

tx-harris-2026-dist185-goldberg-mark.name: Mark Goldberg
tx-harris-2026-dist185-goldberg-mark.bio: Prosecutor in the Harris County District Attorney’s Office; former Houston City Council member, criminal defense attorney and visiting judge.

tx-harris-2026-dist185-beall-andrea.name: Andrea Beall
tx-harris-2026-dist185-beall-andrea.bio: Felony Chief in the Child Fatality Division of the Harris County District Attorney’s Office and adjunct professor at South Texas College of Law Houston.

tx-harris-2026-dist208-armstrong-beverly.name: Beverly D. Armstrong
tx-harris-2026-dist208-armstrong-beverly.bio: Judge of the 208th Criminal District Court; former prosecutor in Polk and Galveston counties for over 15 years.

tx-harris-2026-dist209-warren-brian.name: Brian Edward Warren
tx-harris-2026-dist209-warren-brian.bio: Judge of the 209th Criminal District Court since 2019; former Harris County assistant district attorney and criminal defense attorney.

positions.stance: "I treat everyone who appears before me with grace and dignity," seeking to see the complete person, "not just their worst moment."
"I seek empathy in every case," saying justice "requires compassion alongside accountability, understanding alongside fairness."
Says sending someone to prison "should always be difficult and heavy," and that understanding its life-altering effects keeps him thoughtful and careful.
Imposes necessary sentences when someone poses genuine danger, but says many defendants struggling with addiction, mental health, or poverty "need treatment, not just punishment."

tx-harris-2026-dist228-dozier-caroline.name: Caroline Dozier
tx-harris-2026-dist228-dozier-caroline.bio: Judge of the 228th District Court, appointed by Governor Greg Abbott; served over 31 years as a prosecutor in the Harris County District Attorney’s Office.

tx-harris-2026-dist230-morton-chris.name: Chris Morton
tx-harris-2026-dist230-morton-chris.bio: Judge of the 230th Criminal District Court since 2019; former assistant district attorney and criminal defense attorney.

tx-harris-2026-dist232-silverman-chuck.name: Chuck Silverman
tx-harris-2026-dist232-silverman-chuck.bio: Associate judge in Sugar Land and Missouri City; former judge of the 183rd Criminal District Court.

tx-harris-2026-dist248-overhuls-david.name: David W. Overhuls
tx-harris-2026-dist248-overhuls-david.bio: Attorney in private practice and former Harris County prosecutor.

tx-harris-2026-dist248-unger-hilary.name: Hilary Unger
tx-harris-2026-dist248-unger-hilary.bio: Judge of the 248th Criminal District Court since 2019, with over 30 years as a prosecutor and defense attorney.

tx-harris-2026-dist262-gray-lori.name: Lori Chambers Gray
tx-harris-2026-dist262-gray-lori.bio: Presiding judge of the 262nd Criminal District Court since 2019; previously founding attorney of the Law Office of Lori Gray.

positions.stance: "I believe the Court is the servant of the people, and I approach my duties in this fashion."
"I believe as a Judge, I must provide confidence in the impartiality of the justice system."

tx-harris-2026-dist263-campo-jason.name: Jason A. Campo
tx-harris-2026-dist263-campo-jason.bio: Felony Chief in the Domestic Violence Bureau for Harris County; former Cameron County prosecutor.
